newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA FLOP AGAIN IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA FLOP AGAIN IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIERS.

text.p: Argentina suffered another disappointing result in the World Cup qualifiers on Sunday when they were held to a 1-1 draw at home by a Chilean team reduced to 10 men before halftime.

The Argentines, who had previously lost away to Ecuador, drawn away to Peru and been held at home by Paraguay, needed a penalty converted by Gabriel Batistuta to snatch a point after Fernando Cornejo had given Chile a shock lead.
In a violent, foul-ridden game, Chile had defender Luis Chavarria sent off for a second bookable offence in the 40th minute.

But Argentina threw away their one-man advantage when defender Robeto Ayala was sent off on the hour for elbowing a Chilean player in the face on the touchline, leaving him sprawled against an advertising board.
Argentina have often been accused of violent play in the past but on Sunday they were mostly on the receiving end, the Ayala incident apart.
Chile could have ended the game with seven or eight men on the field had the referee taken the appropriate action against their often wild tackling.
Instead they were let off with five yellow cards and the dismissal of Chavarria, a small price to pay for their tactic of stopping almost every Argentine attack with fouls.
Central defender Javier Margas was especially lucky to stay on the field after committing at least two vicious fouls in the second half.
Striker Ariel Ortega showed outstanding skill for Argentina but his team-mates were not up to the same standard.
After dominating the first half, they fell behind in the 49th minute when Cornejo fired home a free kick from Chile's only decent attack of the game.
Argentina continued to look ineffective but were saved in the 70th minute when Chile gave away a needless penalty, a defender pushing over Ortega when he was running away from the goal.

Batistuta fired home the penalty for his 36th international goal to take Argentina ahead of third-placed Ecuador on goal difference. But it was not enough to save them from being jeered at the end while the small Chilean contingent in the crowd celebrated noisily.

Argentina - 1-Pablo Cavallero, 4-Nelson Vivas (17-Gustavo Lopez, 66th minute), 2-Roberto Ayala, 6-Eduardo Berizzo, 3-Juan Pablo Sorin, 8-Javier Zanetti, 5-Matias Almeyda, 11-Hugo Morales (16-Patricio Campos 66th), 7-Jose Albornoz (18-Abel Balbo 39th), 10-Ariel Ortega, 9-Gabriel Batistuta.

Chile - 1-Nelson Tapia, 2-Cristian Castaneda (17-Wilson Contreras, 64th), 3-Ronald Fuentes, 4-Javier Margas, 5-Pedro Reyes, 6-Luis Chavarria, 7-Cristian Mora, 8-Fernando Cornejo, 14-Victor Castaneda, 22-Sebastiaan Rozenthal (15-Marcelo Miranda, 46th), 11-Marcelo Salas (9-Ivan Zamorano, 78th).
